observation.visible_scene: An indoor kitchen/room corner with a speckled granite countertop. A white sheet of paper lies on the counter, and a small pink spiky (textured) ball is on/above it. A person in a dark t-shirt stands at the left edge of the counter; one hand rests flat on the paper's near edge (fingers spread) and stays there throughout, while the other arm reaches in to handle the ball. A phone/camera sits on the counter in the foreground showing the ball on its screen. Background shows closed white doors and a wall light switch; these stay fixed, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: At the start the pink ball sits low, just above the paper, while the active hand (blurred from motion) descends toward it.
The active hand closes on the ball at the paper surface (roughly frames 5–10) and then lifts it upward off the paper.
From about frame 16 to frame 30 the ball is held pinched in the air at a steady height above the paper, with little vertical change; the resting hand keeps the paper in place.
Around frame 31 the active hand opens and lets go; the ball drops toward the paper.

After the drop the ball moves downward (frames 32–37, with motion blur) and then rises again above the paper (frames 38–41), consistent with a bounce off the paper/counter surface; the released hand remains raised and open at the top of the frame.
The person's reaching arm extends forward and upward as the ball is lifted, then stays high after release; the torso shifts slightly with this arm motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the ball first came to rest on the paper before t=0 (no prior throw or placement is shown).
The outcome after the last frame (whether the ball settles, is caught, or bounces again).
The purpose of the foreground recording device and what is shown on its screen beyond a pink blob.
uncertain_details: Whether the ball in the earliest frames is resting on the paper or momentarily airborne; the blur makes contact timing imprecise.
The exact bounce height and whether the ball touches the paper or just the counter edge is not clearly resolved between frames.
Minor apparent shifts of the ball's horizontal position could be camera/person motion rather than true lateral movement; the background doors look stable, so the camera is likely static.
